cues.zh: 可以！至少在理论上可行。
cues.en: Yes! At least in theory.

cues.zh: 我说的可不是把某个在线游戏的网址放进去，那种你显然做得到。
cues.en: And I'm not talking about just putting the URL to some online game in; you can obviously do that.

cues.zh: 我是说把游戏100%的代码完整地存
cues.en: I mean 100% of the game's code stored entirely

cues.zh: 在其中一个二维码里。
cues.en: on one of these.

cues.zh: 说来虽然令人惊讶，但理论上你完全没有理由做不到。
cues.en: As surprising as it is to say, there theoretically is absolutely no reason you couldn't.

cues.zh: 二维码从技术上讲，就是一种和其他任何介质一样的存储介质。
cues.en: A QR code is technically just a storage medium like any other.

cues.zh: 它和软盘、CD乃至硬盘一样正当合理。
cues.en: It's just as legitimate as a floppy disk, CD, or even hard drive.

cues.zh: 它存不了多少数据，但终究还是数据。
cues.en: It doesn't store much data, but it is data nonetheless.

cues.zh: 要知道，数据存储的门槛其实相当低。
cues.en: Keep in mind the bar for data storage is actually pretty low.

cues.zh: 你也可以手动写出二进制的0和1，或者十六进制字节。
cues.en: You could also manually write out binary zeros and ones or hex bytes by hand.

cues.zh: 效率不高，但从技术上讲你确实存储了计算机数据。
cues.en: It's not very efficient, but technically you've stored computer data.

cues.zh: 虽然二维码最常见的用途是存储ASCII文本，
cues.en: And while a QR code is most commonly used to store ASCII text,

cues.zh: 但它其实也能被用来存储二进制数据。
cues.en: it can actually be made to store binary data as well.

cues.zh: 也就是说，基本上你能存在电脑上的任何东西，都能存进二维码——只要它没超出尺寸限制。
cues.en: Which pretty much means anything you can store on a computer, you can store on a QR code - provided that it fits inside the size limitations.

cues.zh: 那限制到底有多大？
cues.en: How limited are we?

cues.zh: 二维码有各种标准尺寸，最大的是版本40
cues.en: Well QR codes come in various standardized sizes, but the largest is version 40

cues.zh: 能给我们足足一个庞然大物般的
cues.en: which gives us an ABSOLUTELY LEVIATHAN

cues.zh: ……字节。
cues.en: ...bytes.

cues.zh: 对，略少于3 KB。不算多。
cues.en: Yeah, slightly less than 3 KB. It's not much.

cues.zh: 如果你好奇到底有多“不算多”，Windows 10里的这个声音……
cues.en: If you're curious just how not much, this sound from Windows 10...

cues.zh: 一个只持续十五分之一秒的声音，这个声音……
cues.en: A sound that lasts for 1/15th of a second, this sound...

cues.zh: ……是11 KB。没错。
cues.en: ...is 11 KB. Yeah.

cues.zh: 还记得软盘吗？我记得的是这种：3.5英寸高密度软盘。
cues.en: Or remember floppy disks? The ones I remember are these: the 3.5" high-density floppies.

cues.zh: 还记得装Windows 95得用上二十张那种吗？
cues.en: Remember needing like twenty of them to install Windows 95?

cues.zh: 那玩意儿容量是1.44 MB，也就是1,474,560字节。
cues.en: Well, those things are 1.44 MB or 1,474,560 bytes.

cues.zh: 也就是说，仅仅一张这种软盘，就能存下不是一张、不是两张，
cues.en: Which means just one of those floppy disks can store not one, not two,

cues.zh: 而是将近500张版本40二维码的数据量。
cues.en: but almost 500 version 40 QR codes worth of data.

cues.zh: 那……我们真能把一整个游戏塞进一个二维码里吗？
cues.en: So... can we really fit a whole game into just one?

cues.zh: 嗯，虽然图片、音乐、视频，还有……操作系统确实占了不少存储空间，
cues.en: Well, while pictures, music, video, and... operating systems do take up a lot of storage space,

cues.zh: 但简单的代码其实可以出奇地省空间。
cues.en: simple code can actually be surprisingly economical.

cues.zh: 而且虽说 3 KB 已经很小了，可有人做过的游戏比这还小得多。
cues.en: And while 3 KB is pretty small even then, people have made games with far less.

cues.zh: 回想软盘时代，你知道有人把游戏塞进软盘的引导扇区里吗？
cues.en: Going back to floppy disks, did you know that people have managed to fit games into a floppy disk's boot sector?

cues.zh: 如果你不知道那有多小，它只有 512 字节。
cues.en: And if you don't know how small that is, it's only 512 bytes.

cues.zh: 大约是我们这里二维码容量的六分之一。
cues.en: Roughly a sixth of what we're dealing with with QR codes.

cues.zh: 既然能把游戏塞进 512 字节，那塞进 3000 字节自然不在话下。
cues.en: If you can fit a game into 512 bytes, you can fit a game into 3,000.

cues.zh: 或者看看 Atari 2600。
cues.en: Or look at the Atari 2600.

cues.zh: 它的大量卡带只能存 4 KB，所以游戏必须塞进这个容量甚至更小。
cues.en: A huge amount of those cartridges could only store 4 KB, so games had to fit into that or less.

cues.zh: 所以理论上，完全没理由不能把一个完全
cues.en: So in theory, there's absolutely no reason we couldn't store a perfectly

cues.zh: 可玩——虽然有点简陋——的游戏存进一个二维码里。
cues.en: playable - if somewhat basic - game onto a QR code.

cues.zh: 那就开始吧！
cues.en: So let's do it!

cues.zh: 我们的第一个决定是写什么游戏，既然这只是为了科学，我们不妨实现一个已经存在的游戏。
cues.en: Our first decision is what game to write, and since this is just for science, we may as well implement something that already exists.

cues.zh: 我常选的简单游戏是俄罗斯方块——我超爱俄罗斯方块。
cues.en: My go-to simple game is Tetris - I love Tetris.

cues.zh: 但我已经讲过俄罗斯方块公司有多爱打官司了。
cues.en: But I've already talked about how litigious the Tetris company can be.

cues.zh: 而且既然我想让这个二维码对公众开放，我绝不会碰那个。
cues.en: And since I'd like to make this QR code available to the public, I ain't goin' near that.

cues.zh: 我要选一个任何拥有过这东西的人都会满怀深情回忆的游戏。
cues.en: I'm gonna go for the game that anyone who had one of these will undoubtedly remember fondly.

cues.zh: 没错，独一无二的……
cues.en: That's right, the one and only...

cues.zh: 贪吃蛇。
cues.en: Snake.

cues.zh: 极其简单，但在智能手机出现之前的时代，它依然足够有趣，能打发无聊。
cues.en: Extremely simple but still just fun enough to fend off boredom in the pre-smartphone era.

cues.zh: 我们的下一个决定是平台，虽然写一个智能手机应用看起来显而易见，
cues.en: Our next decision is platform, and while it seems obvious to write a smartphone app,

cues.zh: 因为如今二维码通常就是用来干这个的，
cues.en: since that's what QR codes are usually used for nowadays,

cues.zh: 但我有些怀疑自己能否在移动端的体积限制内做出东西来。
cues.en: I have some doubts that I'll be able to make something within the size limitations on mobile.

cues.zh: 另外，我觉得智能手机更封闭的特性会让从二维码运行可执行文件难得多。
cues.en: Additionally, the more locked down nature of smartphones I think would make it a lot harder to get an executable to run from a QR code.

cues.zh: 现在想想，这大概是件好事。
cues.en: Which is probably a good thing now that I think about it.

cues.zh: 所以我干脆把它做成 Windows 应用，
cues.en: So I'm just gonna make this a Windows app instead,

cues.zh: 思路是你可以用电脑的摄像头读取二维码。
cues.en: with the idea being that you could read the QR code from the computer's webcam.

cues.zh: 把整个 Windows 可执行文件塞进那 2900 多字节里。
cues.en: Fitting an entire Windows executable into those 2,900-whatever bytes.

cues.zh: 不过在讲这个之前，我先提一个非常简单的实现方式。
cues.en: Before we get to that though, I will mention a really easy way you could pull this off.

cues.zh: 你直接用 HTML 和 JavaScript 写就行。
cues.en: You could just write it in HTML and JavaScript.

cues.zh: 其实，为了演示，我还真写了！
cues.en: In fact, just for demonstration, I did!

cues.zh: 这是用 JavaScript 写的贪吃蛇，当然还配了些 HTML 和 CSS 把它们整合起来。
cues.en: This is Snake written in JavaScript, with some HTML and CSS to pull it all together of course.

cues.zh: 经过压缩之后，也就是基本删掉所有非必需的内容，
cues.en: Once it's been minified, which basically means removing everything not strictly required,

cues.zh: 它刚好能塞进我们二维码的大小限制里。
cues.en: it fits snugly into our QR code size limit.

cues.zh: 你会发现我甚至还加入了一些舒适性功能，比如
cues.en: You'll notice I was even able to fit some comfort features in, like

cues.zh: 编写额外的代码，把蛇画得又长又细，而不是一大团白色方块或圆点，
cues.en: writing extra code to draw the snake as long and thin rather than a big blob of white squares or dots,

cues.zh: 或者把按键排队，这样如果你快速连续按键，它们仍然会被识别到，
cues.en: or queuing up button presses so that if you press buttons in quick succession, they'll still get recognized,

cues.zh: 还有在你即将游戏结束时，给你额外一次宽限回合来移动。
cues.en: and giving you one extra grace turn to move if you're just about to game over.

cues.zh: 就像老式手机过去做的那样。
cues.en: Just like the old phones used to do.

cues.zh: 所以从技术上讲，我们其实已经差不多完成了。
cues.en: So technically we're already sort of done.

cues.zh: 但这感觉有点像作弊，对吧？
cues.en: But it kind of feels like cheating, right?

cues.zh: 虽然这确实是真正的代码，而不只是一个网站URL之类的，
cues.en: While it is actual code and not just a website URL or something,

cues.zh: 你仍然需要安装一个现代浏览器，而这……
cues.en: you still need a modern browser installed which...

cues.zh: 等等，那不是现代浏览器，把它拿出去！
cues.en: Wait that's not a modern browser, get that out of here!

cues.zh: 所以是的，现代浏览器，说实话，它们有点在替我们做很多工作。
cues.en: So yeah, modern browsers, which - let's be honest - are kind of doing a lot of the work for us.

cues.zh: 不知怎么的，就是感觉不对劲。
cues.en: Somehow it just didn't feel right.

cues.zh: 所以我们要把它做成一个原生可执行文件。
cues.en: So we're gonna make this a native executable.

cues.zh: 乍一看，这似乎是不可能的。
cues.en: At first glance, this would appear to be impossible.

cues.zh: 一个用 C 写的超级简单的“Hello World”程序就已经占用了 100 KB。
cues.en: A super simple "Hello World" program written in C already consumes 100 KB.

cues.zh: 但其中大部分其实根本不是我们的代码，而是编译器默认链接的所有运行时库。
cues.en: But most of this is actually not our code at all, it's all the runtime libraries that the compiler is linking by default.

cues.zh: 我们可以用 /NODEFAULTLIB 选项禁用这些，但这确实意味着我们必须手动指定需要的库，
cues.en: We can disable this with the /NODEFAULTLIB option, which does mean that we have to specify the libraries we do need manually,

cues.zh: 不过这样做能把文件大小一路降到 3 KB。很好的开端。
cues.en: but doing this cuts the file size all the way down to 3 KB. A great start.

cues.zh: 现在我们也许可以用更多编译器选项进一步缩小，但我真正要尝试的是完全放弃 C 编译器，
cues.en: Now we could probably get it down further with more compiler options, but what I'm actually gonna try is forgoing the C compiler entirely,

cues.zh: 然后用 x86 汇编来写这个东西……
cues.en: and writing this thing...

cues.zh: ……用 x86 汇编。
cues.en: ...in x86 assembly.

cues.zh: 是的，通常尽可能接近原始机器码。
cues.en: Yep, as close to the raw machine code as is generally possible.

cues.zh: 我在《超级马里奥64》编译器优化那期视频里提到过这一点。
cues.en: I touched on this in videos like my Super Mario 64 compiler optimizations video.

cues.zh: C 代码虽然对外行人来说看起来很技术化，
cues.en: C code, while it may look technical to the uninitiated,

cues.zh: 但它其实非常注重对人类友好。
cues.en: is very much designed to be human friendly.

cues.zh: 要让你的计算机运行它，必须由编译器把它翻译成机器码，
cues.en: For your computer to run it, it must be translated into machine code by a compiler,

cues.zh: 虽然编译器通常很擅长自己的工作，但它们仍然不完美，
cues.en: and while compilers are generally very good at what they do, they're still not perfect,

cues.zh: 最重要的是，它们不是人。
cues.en: and most importantly, they're not human.

cues.zh: 它们无法真正思考如何最好地翻译和优化你的应用。
cues.en: They can't really think about the best ways to translate and optimize your app.

cues.zh: 它们只能做开发者告诉它们要做的事。
cues.en: They can only really do what their developers have told them to do.

cues.zh: 因此，通常人类总能写出比编译器更轻量、更快的机器码。
cues.en: As such, generally a human will always be able to write lighter and faster machine code than a compiler.

cues.zh: 这就是为什么大多数电子游戏直到90年代中期左右，几乎都是用汇编语言编写的。
cues.en: Which is why most video games, up until the mid-90s or so, were almost always written in assembly.

cues.zh: 编译器引入的轻微低效，对那个时代的硬件性能来说实在是太不利了。
cues.en: The slight inefficiencies introduced by compilers was just too detrimental to performance on the hardware of that era.

cues.zh: 现在我打算写一个极其简单的游戏，并在现代硬件上运行，所以性能显然不是什么问题。
cues.en: Now I'm planning to write an extremely simple game and run it on modern hardware, so clearly performance isn't really an issue.

cues.zh: 但用汇编编写也让我们能很好地控制二进制文件的大小，因为我们基本上是在自己写每一个字节。
cues.en: But writing in assembly also gives us a lot of control over the size of the binary since we're kind of writing all the bytes ourselves.

cues.zh: 所以尽管我对C熟悉得多，这看起来确实是该走的路。
cues.en: So even though I am a lot more familiar with C, this really seems like the way to go.

cues.zh: 在完全没有外部帮助的情况下，我很快就写好了一个使用Win32 API创建窗口的汇编程序。
cues.en: And with absolutely no outside help at all, I soon had an assembly program that uses the Win32 API to make a window.

cues.zh: 而且全都在2.5 KB以内。
cues.en: And all within 2.5 KB.

cues.zh: 其实我们已经非常接近上限了，而且还没写任何游戏代码。
cues.en: Yeah we're actually already pretty dangerously close to our limit and we haven't even written any game code yet.

cues.zh: 我删掉了几行不必要的代码，结果发现文件大小一下子降到了2 KB。
cues.en: I trimmed a few unnecessary lines out and found the file size had jumped all the way down to 2 KB.

cues.zh: 这比我实际删掉的代码多得多。
cues.en: That's way more code than I actually removed.

cues.zh: 我把那些行加回去，它又跳回了2.5 KB。奇怪。
cues.en: When I put the lines back, it jumped back up to 2.5. Weird.

cues.zh: 所以原来Win32 PE格式——如今几乎所有Windows可执行文件用的都是这个格式——默认按512字节对齐。
cues.en: So it turns out the Win32 PE format, which is the format of pretty much all Windows executables these days, is by default aligned to 512 bytes.

cues.zh: 而且它还被列为可能的最小对齐值。
cues.en: And it's also listed as the minimum alignment possible.

cues.zh: 这让我有点紧张，因为这意味着我们不仅要把代码控制在2.88 KB以下，
cues.en: This made me a little nervous since it means we don't just have to get our code below 2.88 KB,

cues.zh: 实际上还得压到2.5 KB以下，因为一旦超过就会向上取整到3。
cues.en: we actually have to get it below 2.5 since anything over will round up to 3.

cues.zh: 我还是继续做了，直到屏幕上出现一个可以四处移动的白点，但那时我已经到3 KB了。
cues.en: I went ahead anyway until I had a white dot that could be moved around the screen, but I was already at 3 KB.

cues.zh: 已经超出限制了，游戏内容却还少得可怜。
cues.en: Already over our limit with still barely any game.

cues.zh: 那么……就这样了？
cues.en: So... is that it then?

cues.zh: 也不完全是，512 或许是默认值，甚至是文档写明的最小值，
cues.en: Well not quite, 512 maybe the default and even the documented minimum,

cues.zh: 但 Windows 实际上几乎接受任何值。
cues.en: but Windows will actually accept almost any.

cues.zh: 我们只需要在链接器里覆盖默认值。
cues.en: We just need to override the default in our linker.

cues.zh: 可惜对我来说，我一直在用的链接器似乎没有字节对齐选项。
cues.en: Unlucky for me, the linker I've been using doesn't seem to have byte alignment options.

cues.zh: 我之前用这个是因为它能超级方便地链接现有的 Win32 DLL，
cues.en: I was using this one since it made it super easy to link with existing Win32 DLLs,

cues.zh: 但既然大小是优先考虑，看来我们得换一个了，
cues.en: but seeing as size is a priority, it looks like we'll have to swap out with another,

cues.zh: 这意味着我不得不对代码做些改动。
cues.en: which meant having to make some changes to my code.

cues.zh: 幸运的是改动不太难，很快我们就用上了 MSVC 来链接。
cues.en: Luckily they weren't too hard and soon we were linking with MSVC.

cues.zh: 我没法移除字节对齐，只能把它降到 16 字节，因为我用的 Win32 库就是这种对齐。
cues.en: I couldn't remove the byte alignment, I could only reduce it to 16 bytes since that was the alignment of the Win32 libraries I was using.

cues.zh: 不过这样还是压到了 2.66 KB，确实有进步。
cues.en: But that still got us down to 2.66 KB which is definitely an improvement.

cues.zh: 可惜的是，没过多久又再次撞上了上限。
cues.en: Unfortunately, it still didn't take long to reach the limits once again.

cues.zh: 2.9 已经超了，而我们到现在还 barely 算得上有个游戏。
cues.en: 2.9 is already over and we still only barely have a game here.

cues.zh: [呼气] 你知道，人总有时候得承认自己的局限。
cues.en: [exhales] You know, there comes a time when one must acknowledge their limitations.

cues.zh: 是的，严格来说我会写 x86 汇编，但我真的清楚自己在干什么吗？
cues.en: Yes, technically I can write x86 assembly, but do I really know what I'm doing?

cues.zh: [低声] 不清楚……
cues.en: [whispers] No...

cues.zh: 我知道所有能把二进制做到最小的技巧或最佳实践吗？并不尽然。
cues.en: Do I know all of the tricks or best practices to make the smallest binaries possible? Not really.

cues.zh: 我大概比 C 编译器的开发者们懂得少得多。
cues.en: I probably know a lot less than the developers of a C compiler do.

cues.zh: 我确信我可以去学，但那样我们估计又要再耗上几个月。
cues.en: And I'm sure I could learn them, but then we'd be here for another few months I'm sure.

cues.zh: 我决定自己这是贪多嚼不烂了，而且我也很好奇，如果以正确的方式配置 C 编译器，
cues.en: I decided I'd bitten off more than I could chew here, and I was curious to see if a C compiler set up the right way,

cues.zh: 它能不能比我写出更高效的汇编代码。
cues.en: would be able to write more efficient assembly code than me.

cues.zh: 于是我用C重写了所有东西，其实比听起来容易，
cues.en: So I rewrote everything in C, which was actually easier than it sounds,

cues.zh: 没错，这基本就说明一切了。
cues.en: and yep, that pretty much says it all.

cues.zh: 所以理论上，人类总能写出比编译器更好的汇编代码，但这并不一定意味着他们真的会这么做。
cues.en: So while theoretically a human being can always write better assembly code than a compiler, that doesn't necessarily mean that they will.

cues.zh: 所以我决定继续用C。我用C更顺手，也更相信自己能写出比汇编更干净的C代码。
cues.en: So I decided to carry on in C. I'm much more comfortable with it and I just have more faith that I could write cleaner C code than I could assembly code.

cues.zh: 整个过程我一直密切关注可执行文件的大小，这本身就挺让人紧张的，因为
cues.en: The whole time I was keeping a close eye on the executable size, which in itself was pretty nervewracking since

cues.zh: 现在一切都得看编译器的脸色了。
cues.en: it was now all at the mercy of the compiler.

cues.zh: 一行新的C代码可能增加几个字节到几百个字节不等，
cues.en: A single new line of C code could add anywhere from a few bytes to a few hundred,

cues.zh: 而我一直在想办法用更少的代码做更多的事。
cues.en: and I was constantly trying to find ways to do more with less code.

cues.zh: 但最终，终究还是……
cues.en: But finally, eventually...

cues.zh: ……我失败了。
cues.en: ...I failed.

cues.zh: 我把贪吃蛇做成了我想要的样子，但可执行文件有 3.1 KB——远超 2.88。
cues.en: I got Snake working just how I wanted it to but my executable was 3.1 KB - way more than 2.88.

cues.zh: 我确实写进了那些舒适性功能——绘图代码、按钮排队、短暂的咬合宽限期——
cues.en: I did write in my comfort features - the drawing code, the button queuing, the brief bite grace period -

cues.zh: 我也确实尝试过牺牲这些功能，想把它压到 3.1 以下。
cues.en: and I did play around with compromising these things to try to get it below 3.1.

cues.zh: 但那样做总是让游戏的可玩性大打折扣。
cues.en: But doing that always made the game feel a lot less playable.

cues.zh: 我知道在这种极端的体积限制下，这种牺牲是必须的，
cues.en: I know that is the kind of sacrifice you have to make with extreme size limitations like these,

cues.zh: 但我觉得在开始砍代码之前，应该还能在其他地方做更多。
cues.en: but I felt like there had to be more I could do elsewhere before I started cutting code out.

cues.zh: 虽然这整个东西只是个二维码实验，但我真心希望你能玩到的游戏至少还像样。
cues.en: Even though this whole thing is just a QR code experiment, I really hoped the game you would get would be at least kinda decent.

cues.zh: 于是我开始寻找其他缩小二进制文件的途径。
cues.en: So I started looking at other avenues of shrinking down the binary.

cues.zh: 我们只需要大约200字节左右。
cues.en: We only need about 200 bytes or so.

cues.zh: 我研究了一些相当复杂的非官方修改方法，可以修改PE头，但全都超出了我的理解范围。
cues.en: I looked into some pretty complicated unofficial modifications you could make to the PE header, but the all kinda went over my head.

cues.zh: 而且它们还可能破坏与某些Windows版本的兼容性。
cues.en: And they could also potentially break compatibility with some versions of Windows.

cues.zh: 就在这时，我开始考虑压缩。
cues.en: It was at this point I started thinking about compression.

cues.zh: 这确实感觉有点像作弊，但既然我不想削减功能，这似乎成了唯一的选择。
cues.en: It did feel a little like cheating, but seeing as I didn't want to cut functionality, it looked like it was going to be the only choice.

cues.zh: 我不想把它放进zip里，因为我希望体验直接拿到一个可执行文件就能运行的感觉。
cues.en: Now I didn't want to put it in a zip, because I wanted the experience of just getting an executable and running it.

cues.zh: 不需要解压或其他任何操作。
cues.en: No unzipping or anything else required.

cues.zh: 但幸运的是，还有其他压缩方法，尤其是针对可执行文件。
cues.en: But luckily there are other ways to compress, particularly when it comes to executables.

cues.zh: “可执行文件打包”是一种压缩可执行文件的方式，然后将其附加到一个小型解压程序上，
cues.en: "Executable packing" is a means of compressing an executable and then attaching it to a small decompressor program

cues.zh: 该程序在启动时解压并运行原始程序。
cues.en: that unpacks and runs the original program on startup.

cues.zh: 对用户来说，这完全无感，看起来就像你在运行一个普通应用。
cues.en: To the user, this is completely transparent and just looks like you're running an ordinary app.

cues.zh: 压缩技术在演示场景中被大量使用，用来做出极小的演示程序。
cues.en: Compression is heavily used in the demoscene to make really tiny demos.

cues.zh: 我在这里展示的是 64 KB、4 KB 甚至 1 KB 的演示程序。
cues.en: 64 KB, 4 KB, or even 1 KB demos which I'm showing here.

cues.zh: 我把可执行文件压缩看作演示场景里的“自动调音”。
cues.en: I look at executable packing as kind of like the Auto-Tune of the demoscene.

cues.zh: 是的，严格来说这有点像作弊，但它也是相当聪明的技术，而且
cues.en: Yes it's technically kind of cheating, but it's also really clever technology, and

cues.zh: 大家都在用，所以如果你不用，就等于自废武功。
cues.en: everyone's using it so you're kind of crippling yourself if you don't use it.

cues.zh: 一开始我试了 UPX，因为那是我唯一已经熟悉的工具。
cues.en: First, I tried UPX since that was the only one I was already familiar with.

cues.zh: 但它不支持我自定义的对齐方式，而禁用它之后，我们的 Snake 程序膨胀到了 4.5 KB，
cues.en: But it didn't like my custom alignment and disabling it blew our Snake program up to 4.5 KB,

cues.zh: UPX 也只能把它压到 4。
cues.en: which UPX could only shrink to 4.

cues.zh: 是啊，讽刺的是，这意味着压缩反而让我们的文件变大了。
cues.en: Yeah ironically this means compression has made our file larger.

cues.zh: 但很快，我发现了我本该使用的程序。就是那个demoscene用的：
cues.en: But soon, I discovered the program I should have been using. The same one that the demoscene uses:

cues.zh: Crinkler。
cues.en: Crinkler.

cues.zh: 它在我们编译链中取代了链接器的位置，所以又一次我们换了链接器。
cues.en: This takes the place of the linker in our compile chain so once again we're swapping linkers.

cues.zh: 不过这基本上是个即插即用的替代品，所以这次我没遇到什么问题。
cues.en: This was pretty much a drop-in replacement though so I had no issues this time.

cues.zh: 有了Crinkler加入工具链，我们的Snake程序从3.1 KB缩小到了不到1.4 KB！
cues.en: With Crinkler in the toolchain, our Snake program went from 3.1 KB to just under 1.4!

cues.zh: 整个Snake还不到原来一半的大小！
cues.en: All that Snake in less than half the size!

cues.zh: 二维码的梦想还在继续！
cues.en: The QR code dream lives on!

cues.zh: 我感觉如果我们把它拿回汇编，懂行的人
cues.en: I have a feeling if we took it back to assembly, someone who knew what they were

cues.zh: 应该能在不妥协、不压缩的情况下把它缩小。
cues.en: doing would be able to shrink it down with no compromise and no compression.

cues.en: But instead you're watching me.

cues.zh: 但我要说，我觉得越小越好。
cues.en: But I will say I think the smaller it is the better.

cues.zh: 这意味着二维码可以更小，软件读取起来可能也更容易。
cues.en: It means the QR code can be smaller and probably easier for the software to read.

cues.zh: 你可能会问，那我们怎么创建二维码呢？
cues.en: Speaking of which, how do we create a QR code you may ask?

cues.zh: 用我最喜欢的一些东西：Unix 命令行工具。
cues.en: Well with some of my favorite things in the world: Unix command line utilities.

cues.zh: 首先，我用一个叫 qrencode 的工具把二进制数据转成二维码。
cues.en: First, I'll use a tool called qrencode to convert our binary data into QR.

cues.zh: 得告诉它我们的数据是二进制的，否则它会默认当成文本。
cues.en: We'll have to tell it our data is binary since it will otherwise assume it is text.

cues.zh: 完成了——连一秒都用不到。
cues.en: And it's done - doesn't even take a second.

cues.zh: 就是这样。一整个贪吃蛇游戏就在二维码里。
cues.en: There it is. An entire Snake game inside a QR code.

cues.zh: 这就是我们一直等待的时刻，终于到了。
cues.en: This is what we've been waiting for this whole time and we're finally here.

cues.zh: 现在进行终极测试，我们能把可执行文件还原回来吗？
cues.en: And now for the ultimate test, can we get our executable back?

cues.zh: 为此，我会用另一个叫 ZBar 的工具。
cues.en: For this, I'll be using another tool called ZBar.

cues.zh: 它能读取各种条形码，包括二维码，有两种形式：
cues.en: It reads all sorts of barcodes, including QR codes, and comes in two forms:

cues.zh: zbarimg 用于图片，zbarcam 用于摄像头。
cues.en: zbarimg for images and zbarcam for webcams.

cues.zh: 我先用 zbarimg 试试我们原来的二维码图片。
cues.en: I'll try zbarimg first with our original QR code picture.

cues.zh: 我们得再次告诉它，我们的代码里是二进制数据，不是文本。
cues.en: Once again, we'll have to tell it that our code contains binary data rather than text.

cues.zh: 好，看起来不错……
cues.en: Okay, looks good...

cues.zh: 没错，完美解码了！
cues.en: And yep, it decoded perfectly!

cues.zh: 我们现在运行的这个可执行文件，就是从二维码解码出来的。
cues.en: This executable that we're playing right now was just decoded from a QR code.

cues.zh: 接下来是终极、终极测试。
cues.en: And now it's time for the ultimate, ultimate test.

cues.zh: 二维码的意义就在于，它能用摄像头从现实世界中轻松扫描进来。
cues.en: The whole point of a QR code is that it can be easily scanned in from the real world with just a camera.

cues.zh: 那我现在就把它打印出来。
cues.en: So here I go printing it out.

cues.zh: 现在启动 zbarcam……
cues.en: Now let's fire up zbarcam...

cues.zh: 呃，好丑，那是谁？
cues.en: Eww gross, who's that?

cues.zh: 它花了一会儿才识别出来，但最终还是生成了一个可执行文件。
cues.en: It took a moment to recognize, but it eventually made an executable.

cues.zh: 然后……
cues.en: And...
Oh...
Huh...

cues.zh: 它不工作。
cues.en: It doesn't work.

cues.zh: 也许只是没读对？
cues.en: Maybe it just didn't read properly?

cues.zh: 纸不平整似乎确实让它有点吃力，所以我试着用硬纸板把它撑平。
cues.en: It did seem to have some trouble with the paper not being flat, so I tried to use cardboard to keep it straight.

cues.zh: 不行，还是……坏的。
cues.en: No it's... still broken.

cues.zh: 怎么回事？从图片里读完全没问题，但从摄像头读就不行？
cues.en: What happened? It read perfectly fine from the image but not from the webcam?

cues.zh: 肯定有问题。我从命令行运行时，它只报段错误，所以肯定是在某个地方被破坏了。
cues.en: Something's definitely wrong. When I run it from the command line, it just says segmentation fault, so it must be getting corrupted somewhere.

cues.zh: 我们当时就差那么一点了！
cues.en: We were so damn close!

cues.zh: 我决定创建一个新的二维码，把纠错级别调高。
cues.en: I decided to create a new QR code with the error correction turned up.

cues.zh: 之前是低级别，现在我设成Q，这是还能装得下的最高级别。
cues.en: Before it was set to low, I'm setting it to Q which is the highest that can still fit.

cues.zh: 纠错本身需要更多数据，所以能容纳的量是有限的。
cues.en: Error correction inherently requires more data so there is a limit to how much we can have.

cues.zh: 我本来没指望这能有多大用，因为二维码纠错更多是为了应对码被刮花或损坏的情况。
cues.en: I didn't expect this to do much since QR code error correction is intended more for if the code gets scratched or damaged somehow.

cues.zh: 但我还是得试试。
cues.en: But I had to try it.

cues.zh: 嗯？
cues.en: Ehh?

cues.zh: 不行，还是没用。
cues.en: Nope, still not working.

cues.zh: 太奇怪了。它怎么能从原始图片完美解码，现在却不行？
cues.en: This is so weird. How could it decode perfectly from the original image but not now?

cues.zh: 我决定拿出十六进制编辑器，把两个可执行文件并排对比。
cues.en: I decided to bring out the hex editor and compare the executables side by side.

cues.zh: 一看就立刻明白问题出在哪了。
cues.en: From there it was immediately clear what was wrong.

cues.zh: 看到原始文件里这个 0A 字节了吗？
cues.en: You see this 0A byte here in the original?

cues.zh: 而从二维码里取回的可执行文件里，这个字节神奇地变成了两个：0D 和 0A。
cues.en: In the executable retrieved from the QR code, that byte has magically become two: 0D and 0A.

cues.zh: 了解 ASCII 的人已经知道发生了什么。
cues.en: Now those of you who know ASCII already know what's happened here.

cues.zh: 但如果你不知道，想想我们平时是怎么把语言分成段落或换行的？
cues.en: But in case you don't, you know how we often tend to break up language into paragraphs or separate lines?

cues.zh: 计算机可不是由行构成的，它在内部并没有真正实现换行的方式。
cues.en: Well, computers aren't made of lines, they don't really have a way of doing this internally.

cues.zh: 所以文本通常是这样存储的：一长串连续的流，在换行处放一个特殊字符，这样
cues.en: So usually text is stored like this. One long contiguous stream with a special character where the line breaks go so that

cues.zh: 当它把文本画到屏幕上给我们看时，就知道怎么把文本拆成我们划分的那些行。
cues.en: when it draws that text on the screen for us, it knows how to split the text into the lines we made.

cues.zh: 顺便说一句，这不包括自动换行，因为计算机可以即时计算出来。
cues.en: This by the way doesn't include automatic word wrapping since the computer can calculate that on the fly.

cues.zh: 这只适用于换行和分段。
cues.en: This only applies to line and paragraph breaks specifically.

cues.zh: 这个特殊字符叫做“换行符”或“行结束符”，它并不像这样是个点，而是一个你永远看不到的控制字节。
cues.en: This special character is called a "Newline" or "Line Ending" and it's not really a dot like this, it's a control byte you never see.

cues.zh: 但具体是哪个字节很难确定，因为大家无法达成一致。
cues.en: But what byte that is specifically is hard to pinpoint because not everyone could agree on that.

cues.zh: 如今你真正会遇到的换行符只有两种。
cues.en: Today there are only really two line endings you'll ever see.

cues.zh: 基于 Unix 的系统，也就是 Mac、Linux、iOS 和 Android，都使用一个叫做换行符（line feed）的单个字符，
cues.en: Unix-based systems, so Mac, Linux, iOS, and Android, all use a single character called a line feed,

cues.zh: 用十六进制表示就是字节 0A。
cues.en: which is, in hex, byte 0A.

cues.zh: 程序员更熟悉它的写法是反斜杠加 N。
cues.en: Programmers will know this better as backslash-N.

cues.zh: 然而 Windows 历来使用一个两字节的序列。
cues.en: Windows, however, has historically used a two-byte sequence.

cues.zh: 它们也使用换行符，但前面会加一个回车符。
cues.en: They also use a line feed, but it's preceded by a carriage return.

cues.zh: 十六进制的 0D，或者代码里的反斜杠-R。
cues.en: 0D in hex, or backslash-R in code.

cues.zh: 基本上，Unix 换行符长这样，Windows 换行符长这样。
cues.en: So basically Unix line endings look like this and Windows line endings look like this.

cues.zh: 虽然现在大多数软件都能识别这两种换行符，但仍有少数不行。
cues.en: While most software these days can understand both line endings, a handful still can't.

cues.zh: 直到 2018 年，Windows 记事本只认 Windows 换行符，所以有时用它打开文本文件会变成这样。
cues.en: Up until 2018, Windows Notepad only acknowledged Windows line endings, which is why you'd sometimes open text documents with it that would look like this.

cues.zh: 因此，有些程序会自动把换行符转换成你所用系统的格式，这并不罕见。
cues.en: As such, it's not uncommon for some programs to automatically convert line endings to whatever system you're using.

cues.zh: 你开始看出发生了什么吗？
cues.en: Are you starting to see what's happened?

cues.zh: 平时你不会注意到这一点，因为能兼容两种换行符的软件会识别任意一种，
cues.en: Ordinarily you wouldn't notice this since software that handles both will recognize either type,

cues.zh: 而不兼容的软件，在换行符变“正确”之后也就神奇地能正常工作了。
cues.en: and software that doesn't will magically work now that the line endings are "correct".

cues.zh: 但我们的贪吃蛇游戏不是文本文件。
cues.en: But our Snake game isn't text.

cues.zh: 我们知道这一点，但某个地方的程序不知道，还在往精确的机器码里插入回车符。
cues.en: We know this, but something somewhere doesn't and is inserting carriage returns into what's actually precise machine code.

cues.zh: 难怪它一启动就崩溃。
cues.en: It's no wonder it just crashes on startup.

cues.zh: 我们已经知道 zbarimg 能正常解码我们的可执行文件，所以问题一定出在 zbarcam 上。
cues.en: We already know zbarimg can decode our executable fine, so it must be something with zbarcam.

cues.zh: 也许是某种 bug？
cues.en: Some sort of bug maybe?

cues.zh: 开源软件的好处就在于，我们可以深入代码自己看看哪里出了问题，
cues.en: Well the joys of open source software allow us to dive into the code and see what's wrong for ourselves,

cues.zh: 我很快就发现，“stdout”没有被设置为二进制模式。
cues.en: and I pretty quickly found that the "stdout" wasn't being set to binary mode.

cues.zh: 这基本上意味着 zbarcam 没有表明它的输出不是文本，于是 Windows 就假定它是文本。
cues.en: Which basically means zbarcam gave no indication that its output wasn't text, so Windows assumed that it was.

cues.en: Let's fix that up and try it again.

cues.en: Obviously QR codes could always link to malicious websites, but if you can store
